issues.description: Ship partial and full refunds for captured payments. A refund is idempotent on the payment id. A partial refund cannot exceed the captured amount. One ledger line is written per successful refund, and a duplicate request returns that same line. The webhook refund.succeeded must keep the original ledger line when it is delivered twice. The payments service owns capture. This Epic owns the refund API, the ledger line, and the webhook handler.
Reconcile refund ledger lines with the payment provider. This Epic relates to Ship payment refunds. Keep one refund per payment id, and keep a duplicate webhook on the original ledger line.
POST /refunds. The idempotency key is the payment id. A partial amount is allowed up to the captured amount. A repeat request returns the original refund.
Write one ledger line per successful refund. A duplicate refund request returns the original line.

issues.summary: Duplicate refund webhook creates two ledger lines
issues.description: Delivering refund.succeeded twice creates two ledger lines. The handler should treat the payment id as the idempotency key and return the original line.
Refunds require a captured payment. Confirm the capture contract this Epic depends on, and link the blocking issue.
